newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk court requires supervision in BOT investments.
newsitem.headline: Turk court requires supervision in BOT investments.

text.p: Turkey's constitutional court on Thursday required supervision by the Council of State in big infrastructure projects to be made under a model called build-operate-transfer (BOT) which requires the builders to provide finances themselves.
The Anatolian agency said the court annulled a sentence which fully authorised the cabinet to set the details of special contracts to be made with contractors on BOT basis.
With the cancellation, BOT contracts to be signed will be subject to inspection by the Council of State.
A total of 116 opposition MPs had filed the cancellation request.
Turkey opened in late 1996 tenders for 55 small hydraulic power plants to be constructed on BOT basis.

The BOT model was devised in the 1980s to finance big infrastructure projects through foreign-led consortia, but faced bureaucratic obstacles which caused several big energy projects to be delayed for several years.
Another model called build-operate (BO) was introduced last year for thermal plants to encourage private sector energy investments.
